html: If you think you or someone near you is having a heart attack, call 911 instead of driving to the hospital. Paramedics can start treatment on the way, and every minute counts.

• Pressure, tightness or aching in the center of the chest that lasts or keeps coming back
  • Discomfort spreading to a shoulder, arm, the jaw, neck or back
  • Feeling out of breath
  • Breaking into a sweat, feeling sick to your stomach or dizzy

section.sectionHead: It doesn't always look like the movies
html: Some people, especially women, older adults and people with diabetes, have milder or unusual signs, such as sudden exhaustion or nausea with little chest pain. Take these seriously too.

• Keep blood pressure, cholesterol and blood sugar in check
  • Quit smoking
  • Move more and choose heart-friendly foods
